title: Markers with a double quote inside a value are re-quoted wrongly by `str()`, changing their meaning
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

```python
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
s = 'demo; \'a" == os_name or python_version >= "0" or "b\' == os_name'
r = Requirement(s)
r.marker.evaluate()                    # False
str(r)                                 # expected: s, unchanged
Requirement(str(r)).marker.evaluate()  # expected: False
```
Actual: `str(r)` is `demo; "a" == os_name or python_version >= "0" or "b" == os_name`, a different marker that evaluates to `True`. More simply, `str(Marker("os_name == 'a\"b'"))` gives `os_name == "a"b"`, which does not even parse.

PEP 508 allows either quote style around a value. When a marker is written out, a value should use double quotes unless it contains one, in which case single quotes. A value containing both quote characters cannot be written in PEP 508 (this only happens for a marker tree built by hand): writing it must raise `ValueError("Cannot serialize marker value containing both quote characters")` instead of producing wrong text.
acceptance: The reported requirement and marker round-trip through `str()` with the same meaning
Values without a double quote are still written with double quotes
Writing a value with both quote characters raises the `ValueError` above
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
